references.text: The Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness, showing a recurring pattern of the people's complaints during their journey through the desert.
The Lord's anger burned against the people because of their sin with the golden calf, and Moses interceded for them, just as the situation develops in Numbers 11.
Shortly before this event, the people had already complained, and the Lord's anger had burned against them - showing an escalation of discontent.
The people wept again and complained against Moses and Aaron after the report from the spies, demonstrating the same pattern of weeping and complaining in the camp.
The psalm describes how the Lord heard the people's complaints and became angry because they did not trust in God or rely on His salvation.
The psalm tells how the people grumbled in their tents and did not listen to the Lord's voice, which led to God's judgment.
Moses reminds the people of how they grumbled in their tents and said that the Lord hated them - the same situation of complaining at the entrances of the tents.
Paul warns against grumbling as some of the Israelites did, who were killed by the destroyer - a direct reference to events during the wilderness journey.
